kangaroo-at-2015-felix-01.title: Check each shape
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-01.body:
Look for each option in all four pictures.

- Small circle, big circle, small triangle and big triangle are in every picture.
- The green rectangle is in the 1st, 3rd and 4th pictures, but **not** in the 2nd picture.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-01.title: Look at one picture
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-01.body:
It is enough to find a picture where one of the shapes is missing. The 2nd picture has only circles and triangles, so the green rectangle is the shape that is not in every picture.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-02.title: Count from top to bottom
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-02.body:
- The bow in the hair: 2 triangles.
- The nose: 1 triangle.
- The two arms: 2 triangles.

The dress top, the skirt, the belt and the shoes are not triangles (they have 4 sides).

$2 + 1 + 2 = 5$.

**Answer: (C) 5**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-03.title: Match the gap
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-03.body:
Look at the white hole in the house (to the right of the window). Its edges have a bump and a step. Compare the outline of the gap with each piece: only piece E has the same bumps in the same places, so it fits the hole exactly without turning it over.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-04.title: Count each ladybird
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-04.body:
Count the dots on each ladybird: 2, 3, 3, 5 and 6.

$2 + 3 + 3 + 5 + 6 = 19$.

**Answer: (C) 19**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-04.title: Make nice sums
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-04.body:
Add in a clever order: $2 + 3 + 5 = 10$ and $3 + 6 = 9$, so $10 + 9 = 19$.

**Answer: (C) 19**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-05.title: Look at the overlap
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-05.body:
Every long strip is made of two equal strips. The more the two strips overlap, the shorter the long strip is.

The two bolts of a long strip sit at the two ends of the overlap, so the farther apart the two bolts are, the bigger the overlap. In strip B the bolts are the farthest apart, so B has the biggest overlap and is the shortest.

**Answer: (B) B**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-05.title: Count holes
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-05.body:
Each strip has the same number of holes. Count the holes you can see along each long strip: the strip with the fewest visible holes is the shortest. Strip B shows the fewest holes because most of its two strips lie on top of each other.

**Answer: (B) B**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-06.title: Turn the cards
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-06.body:
Turning a card (rotating it in the plane) does not flip it over: a kangaroo looking left with its tail on the right keeps the same order of head, body and tail around the card.

Rotate each card in your mind until the kangaroo stands upright. Cards A to D become mirror images of the given card (the kangaroo faces the wrong way) or have the lines in the wrong places. Only card E, turned a quarter turn, looks exactly like the given card.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-07.title: Look down
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-07.body:
The tower is a cylinder with a cone on top. From exactly above, the cylinder looks like a circle, and the cone sits exactly on the circle, so it is also a circle (with its tip in the middle). You see a circle.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-08.title: Check each number
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-08.body:
The numbers inside the red square are 9, 24, 21 and 36. The numbers outside the square are 52 and 48 (they are inside the circle, but not inside the square).

That is **2** numbers.

**Answer: (E) 2**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-08.title: Count and subtract
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-08.body:
There are 6 numbers in total. 4 of them (9, 21, 24, 36) are inside the square, so $6 - 4 = 2$ are outside.

**Answer: (E) 2**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-09.title: Double it
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-09.body:
The whole journey is two halves. Each half takes half an hour, so the whole journey takes half an hour + half an hour = **1 hour**.

**Answer: (D) 1 hour**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-09.title: Use minutes
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-09.body:
Half an hour is 30 minutes. Two halves of the journey: $30 + 30 = 60$ minutes, which is 1 hour.

**Answer: (D) 1 hour**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-10.title: Count the cubes
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-10.body:
Two blocks of 2 cubes have $2 + 2 = 4$ cubes. Count the cubes in each figure: A, C, D and E each have 4 cubes, but figure B has **5** cubes (4 on the bottom and 1 on top). So B cannot be made.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-10.title: Build them
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-10.body:
Try to split each figure into two pairs of cubes next to each other. A, C, D and E can be split this way. B has an odd number of cubes, so it can never be split into pairs.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-11.title: Share the difference
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-11.body:
Katharina has $17 - 9 = 8$ more sweets than Julia. To make it fair, she gives half of the difference: $8 \div 2 = 4$.

Check: $9 + 4 = 13$ and $17 - 4 = 13$. ✓

**Answer: (C) 4**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-11.title: Find the fair share
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-11.body:
Together they have $9 + 17 = 26$ sweets. Shared equally, each gets $26 \div 2 = 13$. Julia needs $13 - 9 = 4$ more.

**Answer: (C) 4**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-12.title: One tower at a time
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-12.body:
In each tower the colours must alternate, because two cubes of the same colour cannot touch. The top cube of every tower is grey, so each tower is grey, white, grey, white, grey: **2 white cubes** per tower.

Six towers: $6 \times 2 = 12$ white cubes.

**Answer: (C) 12**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-12.title: Count grey first
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-12.body:
Each tower has 5 cubes alternating and starting with grey, so 3 grey and 2 white. All 6 towers: $6 \times 5 = 30$ cubes, of which $6 \times 3 = 18$ are grey, so $30 - 18 = 12$ are white.

**Answer: (C) 12**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-13.title: Match the neighbours
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-13.body:
Each triangle tile shows parts of stars. Where two tiles meet along an edge, the halves of the stars must fit together into whole stars.

Look at the three neighbours of the missing triangle and note which star halves touch the gap on each side. Only piece A has the matching star halves on all three sides in the right places.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-14.title: Count the gaps
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-14.body:
With 11 flags in a row there are $11 - 1 = 10$ gaps between neighbouring flags. Each gap is 8 meters: $10 \times 8 = 80$ meters.

**Answer: (D) 80 meters**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-14.title: Try a small case
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-14.body:
2 flags have 1 gap, 3 flags have 2 gaps, ... so 11 flags have 10 gaps. $10 \times 8 = 80$ meters.

**Answer: (D) 80 meters**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-15.title: Before and after
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-15.body:
The leader is 8th, so 7 pirates climb before him. He is in the middle, so 7 pirates climb after him too.

$7 + 1 + 7 = 15$ pirates.

**Answer: (B) 15**

kangaroo-at-2015-felix-15.title: Check the options
kangaroo-at-2015-felix-15.body:
If there were 16 pirates, there would be no single middle pirate. With 15 pirates the middle one is the 8th (7 before and 7 after). ✓

**Answer: (B) 15**
